subject: Anthropology
title: Exogamy and Endogamy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Exogamy and Endogamy.

hook.text: You must marry outside your clan. Or you must marry within your caste. Marriage rules dictate who is off-limits.

buildup.text: Exogamy requires marrying outside your group. Endogamy requires marrying within it. Both shape social boundaries.

discovery.text: Exogamy builds alliances between groups by forcing intermarriage. Endogamy preserves group identity and resources.

twist.text: Most societies use both. You may be exogamous with your clan but endogamous within your class, race, or religion.

climax.text: Marriage rules are boundary-making tools. They decide who belongs, who connects, and who stays separate.

punchline.text: Who you can't marry matters as much as who you can.

details.summary: Exogamy requires marriage outside one's kin group, clan, or community, while endogamy requires marriage within a defined group. These rules shape genetic diversity, social alliances, and cultural boundaries across societies.
details.whyItMatters: Marriage rules are among the most powerful mechanisms for structuring social life. Exogamy builds alliances between groups while endogamy preserves group boundaries, wealth, and cultural identity.
takeaways: Exogamy mandates marriage outside one's own social group
Endogamy requires marriage within a defined group or category
Both rules shape genetic diversity and social structure profoundly

faq.question: Why do many societies practice clan exogamy?
faq.answer: Marrying outside one's clan creates alliances between different kin groups, building social cohesion across the broader community. It also prevents inbreeding within a descent group. Lévi-Strauss argued that exogamy is the foundation of social organization itself.

faq.question: What are examples of endogamy in modern societies?
faq.answer: Caste endogamy in India restricts marriage within one's caste. Religious endogamy discourages interfaith marriage. Class-based endogamy, though less formal, means people tend to marry within their socioeconomic group. All preserve group boundaries and concentrate resources.
